tex_content.html:
Proposition
[Slice chart of a submersion, Euclidean form]

↗ lem:surjection-splits

Let $E, E'$ be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let $f : E \to E'$ be $C^\infty $ at $a$, and suppose $df_a$ is surjective. Set $G(x) = (f(x), P(x))$, where $P : E \to \ker df_a$ is a continuous linear projection. Then $G$ restricts to a homeomorphism of an open neighborhood $U$ of $a$ onto an open subset $G(U) \subseteq E' \times \ker df_a$; moreover $G$ is $C^\infty $ at $a$ and $G^{-1}$ is $C^\infty $ at $G(a)$, and the first component of $G$ is $f$. Consequently, for every $c \in E'$, \[ G(U \cap f^{-1}(c)) = G(U) \cap \left(\{ c\} \times \ker df_a\right); \] that is, in the coordinates $G$ the level set $f^{-1}(c)$ is the affine slice $\{ c\} \times \ker df_a$, whose second factor is a linear subspace of dimension $\dim E - \dim E'$.

Proof

↗ lem:surjection-splits By Lemma 4, $dG_a = (df_a, P)$ is a linear isomorphism $E \cong E' \times \ker df_a$, and $G$ is $C^\infty $ at $a$ because both components are. The inverse function theorem therefore supplies an open neighborhood $U$ of $a$ on which $G$ is a homeomorphism onto the open set $G(U)$, with $G$ smooth at $a$ and $G^{-1}$ smooth at $G(a)$.

The first component of $G$ is $f$ by construction, so for $x \in U$ we have $f(x) = c$ if and only if the first component of $G(x)$ is $c$, i.e. if and only if $G(x) \in \{ c\} \times \ker df_a$. Thus $U \cap f^{-1}(c) = U \cap G^{-1}(\{ c\} \times \ker df_a)$, and applying the bijection $G|_U$ gives $G(U \cap f^{-1}(c)) = G(U) \cap (\{ c\} \times \ker df_a)$. Finally $\dim \ker df_a = \dim E - \dim E'$ by the rank–nullity theorem, $df_a$ being surjective.

□
